_note: Which repositories get an automatic dependency-bump pull request when this
repository publishes a release, and which surface each one has.
npm   — declares @calimero-network/* packages in some package.json, or
resolves them through a pnpm catalog
cargo — pins calimero-network/core by git tag. Recorded so this file stays
the same shape across every producer; a release HERE never touches
it, and fleet-bump.yml selects npm consumers only
tauri — ships a merod binary rather than linking an SDK. Same: not ours
A repository's DEFAULT BRANCH is deliberately not recorded here. The fleet is
split roughly evenly between master and main, and a hand-maintained table of
which is which is exactly the kind of thing that goes stale and then fails
silently. The workflow checks out whatever the repository says its default
branch is and opens the pull request against that.
Nor is the location of a repository's manifests recorded. bump-fleet.sh finds
every package.json that actually declares the dependency and walks up to the
nearest lockfile, so app/, apps/desktop/, packages/frontend/ and anything
added later all work without being listed.
ONE CONSUMER IS A MONOREPO, AND IT IS NOW MOST OF THE FLEET.
calimero-network/apps holds all sixteen apps that used to be sixteen
repositories. It does not have sixteen of anything: the npm versions live
once in pnpm-workspace.yaml's `catalog:` and fan out to every app under
apps/*/app. A release here is ONE pull request instead of sixteen, and
rewriting the apps' package.json files would change nothing — the literal
string `catalog:` is what they declare.
That is also why the catalog is handled before, and separately from, the
per-manifest walk: `catalog:` carries no digits, so the numeric guard in the
per-manifest path skips it and the run would report `already at the
requested version` and exit 4. A repository that silently stops receiving
bumps while reporting success is the exact failure the exit codes exist to
prevent.
